ITEM 2.  WRITTEN AND ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

  A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Norm Haynie suggested anyone willing to build a 15.000 to 20,000 gallon onsite
  water tank with a draft hydrant to allow fire department use in the event of an
  emergency should be permitted to build a new single-family residence. He noted
  the lack offunding to replace an outdated water tank in the Lower Encinal Canyon
  area with inadequate fire flow and pressure. Replacement would take at least two
  years with additional water use restrictions for residents during that time and there
  was no estimated start date for construction. The Los Angeles County Fire
  Department (LACFD) had allowed water tanks for homes above the pressure zone
  or more than 2.000 feet from a Los Angeles County water main over the past forty
  years. Mr. Haynie stated the Los Angeles County Waterworks District 29 had used
  the LACFD requirements to extort funding for improvements from individual
  property owners.

  Ryan Embree commented on the Planning Commission recommendations to City
  Council regarding temporary use permits and sign permits and expressed concern
  that limitations to coloring. lighting and design of signage were not in the final
  resolution. Assistant City Attorney Martz had commented that these signs would
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutas of June 16. 2025
  Page 3 of 1]

b6 required to comply with the City’s sign ordinance as well. However, the
proposed changes were for an exception ordinance. He asked for more clarity and
specificity in the final language. He cautioned that traditionally a local business
held a July 41" party in violation of the Temporary Use Permit Ordinance. He
suggested the Commissioners ask staff to read aloud the conditions which trigger
the need for a temporary use permit.

Commissioner Kamins stated a political mailer was recently sent anonymously to
all registered voters in Malibu, which specifically named Commissioner Mazza and
resident Jo Drummond and accused them ofethics violations. abuses ofpower, and
the use of inflammatory and defamatory language. The mailer did not include a
campaign finance disclosure and was signed as concerned citizens of Malibu. She
stated the mailer constituted harassment rather than civic engagement and asked for
a city investigation into the source of the mailers. She asked that the author or
authors come forward publicly and expressed concern that it would reduce the
number ofresidents who would serve the city.

Assistant City Attorney Martz clarified that the City would protect First
Amendment rights and those on the dais should exercise caution and respect the
right to anonymity for civic discourse.

Commissioner Mazza stated that the mailer specifically said that he. Jo Drummond.
Steve Uhring and Bruce Silverstein control the city and the development process.
to the detriment of retail businesses in Malibu. He stated that candidates engaged
in smear campaigns during the last election and expressed hope that residents
understood what actually happened within Malibu in the context of commercial
interests versus rcsidcnts’ interests.

Commissioner Peak agreed that the mailers referenced by Commissioner Kamins
were out of line.

COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DIRECTOR REPORT

Principal Planner Eaton formally welcomed newly appointed Community
Development Director Yolanda Bundy and thanked former Interim Planning
Director Tamuri for her service.

Community Development Director Bundy offered her congratulations to Chair
Leonard and Vice Chair Riddick, provided an update on fire rebuild statistics and
notcd upcoming rebuild deadlines and events.

Commissioner Mazza asked for a status update on removal of fire debris for
beachfront properties.
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes ofJune 16. 2025
  Page 4 of 1 1

  Chair Leonard asked for greater detail on the status of construction for Woolsey
  Fire rebuilds with a planning approval and how many ofthose properties had stalled
  in the development process.

  ln response to Chair Leonard. Community Development Director Bundy noted
  roughly one hundred Woolsey rebuilds were in various stages of construction with
  many having submitted requests for revisions. Based on City Council direction,
  staff provided a status report and were able to contact 48 owners to offer support
  through the rebuild process.

  Commissioner Mazza requested an update on debris removal for the properties
  along Pacific Coast Highway which had not yet responded to the City.

  A total of 322 beachfront properties were destroyed in the Palisades Fire. Seventy
  percent of those properties selected opt in and the Army Corps of Engineers had
  completed debris removal for those properties prior to the reopening of Pacihc
  Coast Highway the final week ofMay. A total of l 4 fire destroyed propeity owners
  were not responsive, which included nine beachfront properties, and staff were
  working with the City Attorney’s Office and Los Angeles County to add those
  parcels to the list for Army Corps ofEngineers debris removal by July 7, 2025.

  Chair Leonard asked how long the Army Corps ofEngineers would be available to
  support debris removal efforts within Malibu.

  In response to Chair Leonard, Community Development Director Bundy stated
  they would likely conclude debris removal efforts by the end of the summer. The
  Federal Emergency Management Agency had expressed support for debris removal
  for as many Palisades Fire impacted properties as possible

  The Commission congratulated Community Development Director Bundy on her
  appointment and she expressed her gratitude for appointment and anticipation for
  working collaboratively with the Commissioners in the future.
